manifest.title: Isfahan Intersection Traffic Dashboard
manifest.description: Deep traffic-change, weekly-pattern, approach, graph, map, context, and quality analysis for Isfahan SCATS intersections.

cards.description: Median paired-site change from January 2020 to January 2021; the same calendar month reduces seasonality.
Largest network-wide paired monthly fall in the archive.
Largest paired monthly increase after the March–April low period.
Days with a usable city traffic median inside the 854-day context calendar.
Unavailable channel readings are kept missing; trusted site-months meet both 80% thresholds.
Functional graph built from similarity in weekly traffic profiles.
Graph intersections with medium- or high-confidence coordinate candidates.

charts.title: Network traffic by month
charts.subtitle: Median trusted intersection volume, Oct 2018–Jan 2021; vehicles per 15 minutes
charts.headerMarkdown: This line shows the typical intersection each month. A gap is data that should not be treated as a normal month: November 2020 is missing and December 2020 is partial.
charts.question: How did typical intersection traffic move over the full archive?
charts.rationale: A line chart shows the continuous monthly path and makes the March 2020 break easy to see.

charts.title: Paired month-to-month change
charts.subtitle: Median change for the same trusted intersections in adjacent months
charts.headerMarkdown: Each bar compares the same sites in both months. This avoids a false change caused only by intersections entering or leaving the trusted panel.
charts.question: Which month-to-month movements were large after holding the site set constant?
charts.rationale: Signed bars make the size and direction of each paired movement clear.

charts.title: Month-of-year pattern in 2019
charts.subtitle: Median volume for the same 34 intersections in all twelve months
charts.headerMarkdown: This is the cleanest pre-pandemic seasonality view because it keeps the site set fixed. January is the highest typical month and November is the lowest in this common panel.
charts.question: How much did normal traffic vary by month before the pandemic?
charts.rationale: A common-panel monthly bar chart separates seasonality from changes in which sites report.

charts.title: Daily traffic index
charts.subtitle: Seven-day median; 100 means the matching month-and-weekday level in 2019
charts.headerMarkdown: The index removes normal month and weekday differences using 2019 as the baseline. It still describes traffic; it does not prove why traffic changed.
charts.question: When did daily traffic move away from its normal 2019 pattern?
charts.rationale: A smoothed daily line shows the timing of shocks while keeping the missing-data gap visible.

charts.title: Traffic difference on context days
charts.subtitle: Index-point difference after controlling for Gregorian month and weekday
charts.headerMarkdown: Negative values mean traffic was lower on flagged days than on comparison days. Weather, holidays, events, and COVID policy can overlap, so these are associations, not causal effects.
charts.question: Which external contexts line up with higher or lower traffic?
charts.rationale: A ranked signed bar chart compares factors on the same adjusted index scale.

charts.title: Intersection shock and recovery
charts.subtitle: Each point is one intersection; x = Feb–Mar 2020, y = Apr–May 2020
charts.headerMarkdown: Points farther left had a larger March fall. Points higher up had a larger May recovery. Color shows the functional community, which is based on weekly traffic shape.
charts.question: Did the intersections with the largest March fall also have the largest May recovery?
charts.rationale: A scatter plot shows site-level spread, exceptions, and the relationship between the two changes.
charts.combinationRationale: Color separates functional communities; point size shows normal traffic scale without changing the two change axes.

charts.title: Largest February–March 2020 falls
charts.subtitle: Twelve intersections with the lowest paired change
charts.headerMarkdown: This ranking shows where the March fall was strongest. It is limited to intersections trusted in both February and March.
charts.question: Which intersections had the largest March 2020 decline?
charts.rationale: A sorted horizontal bar makes long intersection names and negative changes easy to compare.

charts.title: January 2021 change from January 2020
charts.subtitle: Eight largest falls and eight largest rises among paired trusted sites
charts.headerMarkdown: Using the same calendar month reduces seasonality. The chart still compares only two points, so use the detail table for the longer history.
charts.question: Which intersections were most different in January 2021 than one year earlier?
charts.rationale: A signed extremes chart keeps both improving and declining sites visible.

charts.title: Traffic index for high-volume intersections
charts.subtitle: Jan 2019–Oct 2020; 100 = each intersection's median 2019 volume
charts.headerMarkdown: The heatmap compares each intersection with its own 2019 baseline. Darker or lighter cells show relative change, not absolute traffic size.
charts.question: Was the 2020 traffic shock broad across large intersections or limited to a few sites?
charts.rationale: A month-by-intersection heatmap shows common timing and site exceptions in one view.
charts.combinationRationale: Each series is one intersection on the same self-indexed scale, so heatmap intensity is comparable across rows.

charts.title: Weekly traffic pattern by hour
charts.subtitle: Network mean volume by weekday and hour; vehicles per 15 minutes
charts.headerMarkdown: This heatmap shows the normal weekly rhythm. Friday is Iran's main weekend day; bright cells show the busiest hours.
charts.question: At what hours and weekdays is traffic normally highest?
charts.rationale: A weekday-by-hour heatmap is the clearest view of a dense 7 by 24 pattern.
charts.combinationRationale: All 24 hour fields use the same vehicle-count unit and form the second heatmap dimension.

charts.title: Intersection 1081 inbound approaches
charts.subtitle: Monthly mean entry-side detector volume by direction
charts.headerMarkdown: North and south carry most of the detected entry volume. These are not exit counts and do not show turning destinations.
charts.question: How did each inbound approach at Intersection 1081 change over time?
charts.rationale: Four lines keep direction-level movement visible without adding incompatible measures.
charts.combinationRationale: Color identifies the four inbound directions on one common vehicle-count scale.

charts.title: Inbound direction mix at busy intersections
charts.subtitle: Twelve high-volume sites with four usable approach groups
charts.headerMarkdown: Each bar totals 100%. The segments show how much detected entry volume comes from south, west, north, and east.
charts.question: How balanced are the four inbound directions at high-volume intersections?
charts.rationale: A 100% stacked bar compares direction mix while removing differences in total site volume.
charts.combinationRationale: The four direction shares use the same denominator and add to 100% for each intersection.

charts.title: Traffic volume and functional centrality
charts.subtitle: Each point is an intersection; centrality is similarity-network weighted degree
charts.headerMarkdown: A central point has many strong links to sites with similar weekly patterns. It is not necessarily a physically central or high-volume road junction.
charts.question: Are high-volume intersections also central in the weekly-pattern graph?
charts.rationale: A scatter plot shows whether traffic scale and functional centrality move together and where exceptions sit.
charts.combinationRationale: Color shows community and point size shows data coverage; both help interpret the volume-centrality relationship.

charts.title: Functional community sizes
charts.subtitle: Number of intersections in each weekly-pattern community
charts.headerMarkdown: Communities group similar traffic rhythms. They are operational peer groups, not administrative districts.
charts.question: How is the functional graph split across communities?
charts.rationale: A simple bar chart shows the size of each mutually exclusive group.

charts.title: Mapped intersection candidates
charts.subtitle: Medium- and high-confidence OpenStreetMap candidates; longitude and latitude
charts.headerMarkdown: This is a coordinate plot, not a road map. Use it to see the spread of mapped candidates; municipal GIS should confirm the locations before planning work.
charts.question: Where are the reliably geocoded functional intersections located across Isfahan?
charts.rationale: A longitude-latitude scatter preserves the spatial pattern without using an unverified basemap.
charts.combinationRationale: Color shows functional community and point size shows traffic scale on the coordinate plane.

charts.title: Source-month temporal coverage
charts.subtitle: Observed 15-minute timestamps divided by expected calendar-month timestamps
charts.headerMarkdown: A value near 100% means the source month is nearly complete. November 2020 is missing; December 2020 has only a small part of the month.
charts.question: Which source months are complete enough to support comparison?
charts.rationale: Monthly bars make missing and partial archive periods impossible to overlook.

charts.title: Trusted-month coverage by intersection
charts.subtitle: Distribution across 74 graph intersections
charts.headerMarkdown: More trusted months means a more stable long-term comparison. A short history does not make a site useless, but its trend is less certain.
charts.question: How much usable monthly history does each intersection have?
charts.rationale: A histogram shows whether coverage is broad or concentrated in a small set of sites.

tables.title: Intersection change and graph detail
tables.subtitle: All 74 graph intersections; use exact values for lookup and follow-up
tables.headerMarkdown: Missing change values mean that the intersection did not meet the trusted threshold in both required months.

tables.title: Most unusual network days
tables.subtitle: Twelve lowest and eight highest daily indexes versus matching 2019 month-weekday baselines
tables.headerMarkdown: An unusual day is a starting point for investigation. The calendar and weather note may explain timing, but it does not prove cause.

tables.title: Functional community summary
tables.subtitle: Traffic-shape groups from the functional similarity graph
tables.headerMarkdown: The most central site has the highest weighted degree inside that community.

tables.title: Source-month quality audit
tables.subtitle: Every archive month, including the missing month added as an explicit row
tables.headerMarkdown: Use this table before reading any sharp monthly change. Low source coverage can look like a traffic change when it is only missing data.

query.description: Monthly and paired-intersection traffic measures built from coverage-normalized SCATS counts.
filters: Mean operational detector coverage is at least 80%.
Headline changes compare the same intersections in both periods.
metric_definitions: Mean 15-minute volume is the coverage-normalized intersection count averaged across valid 15-minute records.
Paired change is later-month volume divided by earlier-month volume minus one, calculated per intersection; the headline is the median site change.
The city monthly line is the median of trusted intersection means for that month.

query.description: Daily city traffic joined one-to-one to Iranian calendar, ERA5 weather, documented events, and national COVID policy fields.
filters: Daily city traffic uses intersections with at least 80% temporal coverage.
metric_definitions: 2019 volume index equals daily city median volume divided by the matching 2019 month-and-weekday median, times 100.
Context effect is the difference in adjusted volume index between flagged and comparison days.

query.description: Intersection traffic summed and counted for each weekday and hour, then aggregated to a network mean.
filters: Only valid coverage-normalized 15-minute volumes are included.
metric_definitions: Hour-of-week mean volume is summed valid volume divided by summed valid observations for that weekday and hour.

query.description: A graph where intersections are connected when their 168-bin weekly traffic profiles are similar.
filters: Graph-eligible intersections have enough hourly-weekday observations for stable profiles.
metric_definitions: Weighted degree is the sum of profile-correlation edge weights touching an intersection.
Community is a group of intersections with more similar weekly profiles inside the group.
DTW cluster groups intersections by the shape of their 24-hour profile, allowing small peak-time shifts.

query.description: Monthly south, west, north, and east entry-side detector volumes derived from the intersection diagrams.
filters: Approach shares use direction-months with at least 80% detector coverage.
metric_definitions: Approach volume is an entry-side detector count near the stop line; it is not a measured exit or turning movement.
Approach share is one direction's mean divided by the sum of the four direction means.

query.description: Medium- and high-confidence geocode candidates matched to graph intersections.
filters: Only medium- and high-confidence candidates with coordinates are shown.
metric_definitions: Map coverage is reliable coordinate candidates divided by functional graph nodes.

sources.label: SCATS source and detector quality audit

query.description: Source-month completeness and channel-level unavailable-reading checks.
filters: SCATS values 2046, 2047, and NA are unavailable; zero stays a valid count.
metric_definitions: Source temporal coverage is observed 15-minute timestamps divided by expected calendar-month timestamps.
Trusted months meet both 80% temporal and detector coverage thresholds.

blocks.body: This dashboard tracks **75 SCATS intersections** from October 2018 to January 2021. The main unit is the coverage-normalized number of vehicles in a 15-minute interval. Use the figures from top to bottom: network change, intersection differences, weekly shape, graph groups, map candidates, then data quality. All changes are descriptive.

## 1. Network change

The largest paired fall was **-25.8% from February to March 2020** across **41 intersections**. The largest rise was **24.4% from April to May 2020** across **43 intersections**. For the longer comparison, January 2021 was **-5.4%** versus January 2020 across **29 paired sites**.

## 2. How individual intersections changed

The next figures keep the intersection as the unit. This shows whether a city-wide movement was broad or driven by a few sites.

All **41 of 41 paired sites fell** from February to March 2020, and all **43 of 43 paired sites rose** from April to May. The correlation between the size of the fall and the later recovery is **-0.07**, which is close to zero. A large fall did not reliably predict a large recovery. **3 sites** have at least one consecutive monthly swing above 50% and are marked for review before the change is treated as operational growth or decline.

## 3. Weekly shape and inbound approaches

Volume says how busy a site is. Shape says when it is busy and which entry direction carries the traffic.

The highest network hour-of-week average is **Thu at 13:00**, at about **806 vehicles per 15 minutes** across the aggregated intersection profile. Friday's average hourly profile is **12.8% lower** than the average of the other six days.
Intersection 1081 fell **-34.2%** from February to March 2020 and rose **27.4%** from April to May. North and south approaches make up **68.9%** of its four-direction mean entry volume.

## 4. Functional graph

The graph contains **74 intersections**, **218 similarity edges**, and **4 communities**. An edge means two weekly traffic profiles are similar. It does not mean the roads touch.

Traffic volume and functional centrality have a Spearman correlation of **-0.04**, which is close to zero. Busy intersections and pattern-central intersections are different operational groups. Intersection 1081 is a good example: it ranks **61 of 74 by volume** but **5 by functional centrality**.

## 5. Spatial view

Only medium- and high-confidence coordinate candidates are shown. The separate interactive Isfahan map remains available in the project output folder.

## 6. Data quality and unusual days

About **20.2% of profiled channel readings are unavailable**. They remain missing and are never randomly filled. November 2020 is missing and December 2020 is partial.

Nowruz days average **18.5 index points lower** than matched comparison days, official holidays average **12.0 points lower**, and wet-weather days average **3.1 points lower**. Friday is not included in this adjusted-factor chart because Friday is itself a weekday; its lower profile is shown in the weekly heatmap.

## Limits

- Detector groups measure **entries near the stop line**, not exits or turning paths.
- Functional edges describe similar weekly patterns, not road links.
- Map points need municipal GIS review.
- Weather, calendar, event, and COVID comparisons are associations, not causal estimates.
- A missing or partial source month is not interpreted as a real traffic fall.
